diagnostic_evidence.quote: The time signals excited at different moments can be separated under the Assumption \ref{sump}.

issues.failure_explanation: The signal emitted at t_j, observed at direction xhat, occupies the time interval t_j - c^{-1} xhat·(D_j + a(t_j)) (and in space-time an expanding shell of thickness ~ diam around D_j + a(t_j)). Non-overlap of consecutive pulses therefore requires a gap condition involving the displacement a(t_j) - a(t_{j-1}), not only diam(D_{j-1})/c. Since Assumption sump only requires |a'| < c (with no margin from c), the stated condition does not imply separation: take c = 1, D_j the unit ball, a(t) = 0.9 t xhat, and t_{j+1} - t_j = 2.5 > 2 = diam(D)/c; then the far-field pulses are supported in [0.1 t_j - 1, 0.1 t_j + 1] and overlap heavily (gap 0.25 versus length 2), and the space-time shells overlap because |a(t_{j+1}) - a(t_j)| + diam(D) = 4.25 > 2.5 = c Δt. Hence the claimed rigorous separability is false in general, and the per-instant data u_j^∞ presupposed in (ISP') cannot be extracted from measured fields under the stated hypotheses.

failure_location.quote: The second assumption ensures that wave signals generated at different instants remain separable due to non-overlapping supports.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the gap hypothesis to a displacement-aware condition, e.g. c(t_j - t_{j-1}) > |a(t_j) - a(t_{j-1})| + diam(D_{j-1} ∪ D_j) (or bound |a'| away from c with a correspondingly enlarged gap), which does imply disjoint wave supports via the retarded potential.
issues.overall_effect: The reduction of the multi-pulse problem (ISP') to single-pulse problems, and hence the applicability of the reconstruction pipeline to moving multi-pulse sources, is unjustified for fast (near-sonic) subsonic motion; the abstract's claim of recovering the excitation instants under Assumption sump is unsupported in that regime. Corollary cor:added-1 is stated for already-separated per-instant data, so its statement is not defeated by this root and is not listed as a dependent.
issues.title: Gap condition in Assumption sump does not ensure separability of pulses from a moving source
issues.why_classification: A contained strengthening of one assumption restores separability and leaves the method and all (separately repaired) conclusions unchanged for slowly moving or well-separated sources; but it narrows the advertised regime of arbitrary subsonic motion with gaps > diam/c, so it is more than a local or typographical fix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Combining \eqref{RIeps}, \eqref{RIf} and \eqref{RIl}, we obtain the range identity
Further, the operator $ {L} : L^2({\color{mgq}D}) \to L^2(0, K)$ is compact with dense range.
the operator $T_{\#}=|\real T| +|\ima T|: X\rightarrow X$ is coercive

issues.failure_explanation: The proof only establishes that F_ε → F and F_{ε,#}^{1/2} → F_#^{1/2} in operator norm, and that each element of Range(L) (resp. Range(F_#^{1/2})) is an L^2-limit of elements of Range(L_ε) = Range(F_{ε,#}^{1/2}). Operator-norm convergence of compact operators does not imply convergence or equality of their ranges, and 'lim Range' is never defined; interpreted as closure of the union, both sides are dense in L^2(0,K) (Range(L) is dense), so the closure statement is trivial and the set equalities (RIf), (RIl) do not follow. The relaxation from |S| ≥ c > 0 to |S| > 0 a.e. destroys precisely the coercivity of T_# that the invoked Theorem A.1 requires, and the truncation argument cannot bridge that gap: in abstract factorizations F = LTL* with T injective but not coercive (e.g. diagonal with eigenvalues tending to 0) one gets Range(F_#^{1/2}) strictly smaller than Range(L), so the identity can fail; no argument excluding this is given.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reinstate the strict positivity |S(x)| ≥ c > 0 on D-bar, under which the cited range identity (Theorem A.1) applies directly and Theorem RH holds; establishing the identity under mere a.e.-positivity would require a genuinely different argument (not supplied in the source).
issues.overall_effect: The Picard-criterion range identity underlying every indicator function (I_η, W_η, h, I, and the uniqueness theorems) is unestablished under the paper's weakened hypothesis |S| > 0 a.e.; the advertised generalization to sources vanishing on null sets (innovation (iii)) is unsupported.
issues.title: Range identity Range(F_#^{1/2}) = Range(L) under a.e.-positive S is unproven: ranges do not pass to operator-norm limits
issues.why_classification: A source-supported repair exists (restore the strictly positive assumption of the cited prior result), which validates the range identity and keeps every formally stated conclusion intact under that stronger hypothesis; the loss is confined to the advertised relaxation. It is not minor because the given limiting argument cannot be patched by a local correction.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: By the choice of $y_m$, the set $\{e^{-i\tau a_m}: m\geq 1\}$ is dense in $L^2(0,K)$.

Choose the set $\{y_m\}_{m=1}^{\infty}$ such that $y=y_1$.Then we have $\phi^{(\hat{x})}_{z,\eta} \in $ Range $(L_N)$ for all $N\geq 1$. By Lemma \ref{lem4.1} (ii), it holds that $\phi^{(\hat{x})}_{z,\eta} \in $ Range $(L)$.

issues.failure_explanation: For u ∈ L^2(D), Lu(τ) = ∫ e^{-iτ s} ρ(s) ds where ρ ∈ L^1(R) is the pushforward density of u dy under the linear map y ↦ c^{-1} xhat·y - t_0, supported in the closed interval c^{-1} xhat·D - t_0. If φ_{z,η}(τ) = e^{-iτ b_{z,η}} equalled Lu on (0,K), the entire functions τ ↦ ∫ e^{-iτ s}ρ(s)ds and τ ↦ e^{-iτ b_{z,η}} would agree on (0,K), hence on R; but the first tends to 0 as τ → +∞ (Riemann–Lebesgue) while |e^{-iτ b_{z,η}}| = 1 — a contradiction (equivalently, F^{-1}φ_{z,η} is the point mass δ_{b_{z,η}}, which no L^1 pushforward density can equal). Thus φ_{z,η} ∉ Range(L) for every z, and the 'if' direction fails on the whole nonempty strip. The proof collapses with it: Range(L_N) = span{e^{-iτ a_m}} is not contained in Range(L), the paper's own density statement gives closure of ∪_N Range(L_N) = L^2(0,K) ≠ Range(L) (a proper dense subspace), so Lemma lem4.1(ii) and (RIfN) are false — norm/density convergence of the operators cannot yield the range equality. Additionally, condition (ii) on {y_m} is unrealizable in dimensions ≥ 2: N balls of radius |D|/N have total volume O(N^{1-d}) and cannot cover the fixed domain D for large N.

failure_location.quote: For any $\eta \in \R$, there holds $z \in {K}_{D,\eta}^{(\hat{x})}$ if and only if $\phi^{(\hat{x})}_{z,\eta} \in $ Range $(L)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Abandon the pointwise test functions and revert to mollified/locally integrated test functions as in the cited earlier approaches, restating and re-proving the range characterization and all downstream indicator and uniqueness theorems for those; no repair preserves the pointwise if-and-only-if statement, which is false.
issues.overall_effect: Every indicator-function characterization is false as stated: via Picard plus Theorem RH, the series I_η^{(xhat)}(y) diverges for all y (even inside the strip), so W_η ≡ 0, and the criteria for the pulse moment t_0 (Th:max), the strip (Th:kd), the Θ-convex hull (TH:hull) and the uniqueness statements (thm:added-1, thm:added-2, cor:added-1) lose their content; the advertised 'rigorous foundation for pointwise test functions' (innovation (ii)) fails.
issues.title: Pointwise exponential test functions never belong to Range(L): the central characterization Theorem lem3.4 is false
issues.why_classification: The section's main theorem is false, not merely unproved: no comparable pointwise range characterization survives, a repair requires replacing the test functions and rewriting every downstream indicator/uniqueness theorem (essentially new proof architecture), and the paper's stated innovation (ii) is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $F^{(\hat x)}$ is a $N\times N$ complex matrix.
In another way,  we may also use the \textcolor{ghx}{SPD} discrete approximation $(F^{(\hat x)})_\#$.

issues.failure_explanation: The claim that (|Re λ̃_n| + |Im λ̃_n|, ψ_n) is an eigensystem of |Re F| + |Im F| presupposes that Re F and Im F share the eigenbasis of F, i.e. (for diagonalizable F) that F is normal. The Toeplitz data matrix (matF) with entries u^∞(xhat, κ + ω_{n-m+1}) is not normal in general — for κ ≠ 0 even the continuous operator is not self-adjoint, and the paper advertises arbitrary frequency bands — so eigenvectors of F need not be eigenvectors of F_# and the stated numbers need not be eigenvalues of F_#. Used literally in (indicator5)–(indicator7), these pairs do not implement the Picard sum for F_# that the theory requires.

failure_location.quote: then one deduces that  an eigen-system of the matrix $(F^{(\hat x)})_\#:= |\real (F^{(\hat x)})|+|\ima(F^{(\hat x)})|$ is $\left\{ ( \lambda^{(\hat x)}_n, \psi^{(\hat x)}_n): n=1,2,\cdots,N \right\}$, where $ \lambda^{(\hat x)}_n:=|\real (\tilde \lambda^{(\hat x)}_n)| +|\ima (\tilde \lambda^{( \hat x)}_n)|$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete the invalid deduction and compute the eigendecomposition of the self-adjoint positive matrix (F^{(xhat)})_# directly — the alternative the paper itself offers in the next sentence.
issues.overall_effect: One of the two stated numerical routes to the eigensystem used in all indicator formulas is mathematically incorrect; implemented as written it computes a spectral decomposition different from the one the Picard criterion needs.
issues.title: Eigensystem of the discrete F_# cannot be deduced from that of F
issues.why_classification: The correct procedure is explicitly available in the same paragraph, so the repair is a local correction of the algorithm description with no change to the method, its guarantees, or any formal result.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The reconstruction results shown in Figures \ref{fig:3-2}(b) and (f) respectively display a straight line at $x=0$.

issues.failure_explanation: In this example D ⊂ {|x| ≤ 1}, t_0 = 4, c = 1, so η_1 = 3 and η_2 = 5. At η = 3 (or 5) the two open strips are K^{(xhat)}_{D,η} = {-2 < x_1 < 0} and K^{(-xhat)}_{D,η} = {0 < x_1 < 2}: they touch but do not meet, so the intersection is empty, not 'a line at x = 0'. By Theorems Th:factorization and Th:max (zero indicator for η ∉ (η_1, η_2)) the indicator W_η vanishes identically at these η. The straight line displayed in the figures is therefore an artifact of the truncated Picard sum, and the claim that it corroborates the theory is false.

failure_location.quote: The width of $K_{D,\eta}^{(\hat{x})} \cap K_{D,\eta}^{(-\hat{x})}$ becomes a line at $x=0$ in theory for $\eta=3$ or $5$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the prose: at η = η_1, η_2 the intersection of the open strips is empty and the theoretical indicator is zero everywhere; describe the observed line as a numerical truncation artifact.
issues.overall_effect: Misstates the theoretical prediction at the critical parameters η_1, η_2 that are used to read off t_0; the reported agreement between numerics and theory at η = 3, 5 is spurious.
issues.title: At η = η₁, η₂ the strip intersection is empty in theory, not 'a line at x=0'
issues.why_classification: A local correction of the numerical discussion; no formal statement, method, or guarantee changes, since the underlying theorems already use the correct open-interval convention.
